publish-boundary-test.ref: server/killSwitchSharing.test.ts (13) + server/publishChokePoint.test.ts (13). socialPublish.ts changed in two ways and both are covered. (1) The kill-switch check was EXTRACTED to killSwitchBlockedPlatforms so igAutopost — an autonomous cron measured at 116 live posts in prod — could share the operator's emergency stop instead of bypassing it. killSwitchSharing.test.ts pins the guard's decisions (global / publishing / per-platform, the DENY audit record naming WHICH switch fired, and the deliberate fail-open when switch state is unreadable) AND pins that the extraction left publishToSocial behaviourally identical — including the partial-block case where one platform is stopped and the other still publishes, which is the behaviour most likely to be lost in an extraction. (2) A `link` field was added, because its absence was WHY nickActions.socialPost reached around the door to metaSocial.socialPost; pinned through to postToFacebook. publishChokePoint.test.ts holds the claim gates at contentAdmin.publishCarousel and nickActions.socialPost, and adds a structural sweep asserting no NEW file can import the low-level publishers — the part that makes it stick, since adStudio was fixed alone on 2026-07-25 and this identical defect survived on three other surfaces. Both structural assertions red-green verified: planting a file that imports postToInstagram fails the sweep by name; removing igAutopost's guard branch while keeping the call fails its pin. CADENCE IS NOT CLAIMED — this change deliberately did NOT apply the feed cap to igAutopost, because policy v7 sets maxFeedPostsPerDay=2 while the autoposter has been doing 3/day on 8 of the last 14 active days, and that conflict is the operator's to resolve, not this PR's to decide silently. PR #1127.

cron-fail-closed.ref: server/__tests__/cron-cadence.test.ts (26), mutation-verified. The cron path changed here is a CADENCE gate, and the new non-operator decision point is claimOncePerShopDay() in server/cron/scheduler.ts — it decides whether a business-hours job may run today. It FAILS CLOSED at every exit: outside business hours -> false; getDb() null -> false; any thrown error -> a log.warn carrying errorId CRON_DAILY_CLAIM_FAILED, then false. That direction is deliberate and asymmetric: two of the four jobs on this path (referral-loop-closer, vip-auto-recognition) send customer SMS, so a DB blip returning `true` would re-fire them on every pass of the 2h tier. A duplicate text costs more than a missed day. The claim also sits INSIDE acquireCronLock(job.name) and releases the lock when it declines — two pods that each read 'not yet run today' would otherwise both claim and both send, which is the v1.7 duplicate-SMS regression this repo already paid for. Tests pin all three properties directly: fail-closed on unreadable claim (asserts the `if (!d) return false` exit and a catch that returns false), the claim-after-lock ordering, and the lock release on a declined claim. Three mutations were verified to turn the suite RED and the file restored byte-identical after each: a businessHoursOnly job moved back into the 24h daily tier (1 fail), the claim moved before the lock (2 fails), and the ET clock replaced by a hardcoded -05:00 offset (5 fails). Full serial suite green: 376 files passed / 2 skipped, 4,622 passed / 50 skipped / 1 todo, exit 0.

operator-walkthrough.ref: DEFERRED, with the reason stated — every change here is on the FAILURE path, and forcing a failure means breaking a read against production. WHAT THE OPERATOR GAINS: a new 'Needs a decision' strip on Today, between the summary cards and Integration freshness, listing cross-domain exceptions the action queue never read — publishing holds, tire orders, membership warnings — plus anything the system could not read, ranked above readable items of the same severity because an unreadable queue could be any size. Empty state says one of two DIFFERENT sentences: 'Nothing outstanding across publishing, tires and memberships' when at least one source actually reported, and 'Nothing measured yet - this is not an all-clear' when none did. WHAT THE OPERATOR STOPS SEEING, three false all-clears on this exact screen, all verified by reading the code: (1) the action queue's empty state tested `filteredQueue.length === 0` and NOTHING else, so a failed work-order read produced a large emerald check saying 'No pending actions in this view' on the same render where the card above already said 'Unable to determine' - and with the type filter set to Work orders it asserted work orders SPECIFICALLY were clear, from a query that had failed; (2) `queueTrustworthy` only inspected the bundle's slices, and work orders are a separate query, so the veto could never fire for them - work orders carry urgency 5 when overdue or blocked, so the highest-priority items were the ones that vanished; (3) PromisesPanel branched on `!open || open.length === 0`, and a failed query leaves `open` undefined, so a dead read rendered 'No open promises.' about the ledger tracking every 'we'll call you back' this shop has made. Also fixed: the 'Active work orders' card rendered a neutral 0 from the same query the card beside it had just declared unreadable, and the capped work-order page now reports '30+' rather than a precise-looking count that is really a lower bound. NOT VERIFIED LIVE: reproducing any of this needs a forced query failure against prod. WHAT IS PROVEN INSTEAD: todayExceptionFeed.test.tsx (16) renders the component and asserts the three empty states, that an unknown outranks a bigger readable count, and that the hide-list ids still exist; adminBundleTruth.test.ts gained pins for the queue empty state and the work-order card. Mutation-verified, restored byte-identical after each: removing the work-order veto fails 1, disabling the PromisesPanel error branch fails 1, treating unmeasured as an all-clear fails 3. FIRST CHECK AFTER DEPLOY: open /admin on the phone and confirm the 'Needs a decision' strip appears under the four summary cards. If it reads 'Nothing measured yet', the ops signal has not loaded — that sentence is deliberately NOT an all-clear and should be treated as a symptom, not a pass.

capability-ledger-updated.ref: capability-ledger.json: NEW capability `admin-signal-ledger` added (45 -> 46). That is the capability this diff creates — a three-state badge model (counted | unknown | not_measured) replacing getBadgeCount(). No existing entry covered admin signal truth. DELIBERATELY NOT PROMOTED: operationalState unit_verified, exposure `internal`, because badge numbers on the HEALTHY path are unchanged by construction and the only visible proof is the FAILURE path — a degraded slice rendering '?' instead of a number — which cannot be forced from a test. The entry carries two P2 blockers (no production observation; 10 of 16 sections still emit no signal, which is the honest state rather than a regression since they previously rendered a fabricated 0) and, unusually, a REJECTED-ON-COST list in deferredScope so the next session does not re-propose sources that adversarial verification already killed: bundle.stats.content.* (three SELECT-all-columns LIMIT 500 queries plus JS filters), bundle.stats.callbacks.* (SELECT * of up to 500 fat rows), bundle.health/getSiteHealth (unbounded SELECT over dynamicArticles, no LIMIT), and instagramAdmin.getPipelineHealth (an expensive duplicate of operationsSignal.heldReels). It also records that `intelligence` and `opsHub` have NO cheap unknown-aware source at all — the finding, not a gap to paper over — and flags that operationsSignal's 'two COUNT(*) queries' docblock may understate its real cost, unverified here and left for its own investigation.
